summary: The study reports on the deposition of crystalline AlN thin films using plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) at 250 1C with trimethylaluminum and nitrogen 5% hydrogen plasma precursors. The films exhibit strong (100) preferred orientation and are characterized by structural, compositional, and optical properties. The optical band gap is 6.04 eV, and the refractive index is 1.96 at 632 nm wavelength. The films show thickness-dependent optical properties, with the refractive index and band gap stabilizing above 30 nm and 15 nm, respectively.
evidence: A plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) process has been used to deposit crystalline AlN thin films at 250 1C using nitrogen 5% hydrogen plasma and trimethylaluminum precursors. The optical band gap, measured using spectroscopic ellipsometry, is 6.04 eV, and the refractive index, measured at 632 nm wavelength, is 1.96. The optical properties were thickness-dependent below 30 nm for refractive index and below 15 nm for band gap.
